source.title: MechELK: A Mechanistic Interpretability Framework for Eliciting Latent Knowledge in Large Language Models
source.authors: Ji-jun Park; Soo-joon Choi; Jiwon Jeong; T. Yoon; Ju-Wan Lee

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether SAE-derived features in LLMs can be recovered and used to read out latent knowledge, an indirect-evidence version in a new setting. It does not test toy-model superposition geometry.
record.gate_note: The paper cites superposition and uses SAEs to elicit latent knowledge. Rows below are limited to its SAE-Probe results and the ablation isolating the SAE component. Its aggregate MechELK results, layer distributions, CKS-threshold and steering-strength sweeps, and paraphrase-direction consistency concern the elicitation pipeline, not superposition geometry or the general completeness of SAE dictionaries. Cited superposition findings are not treated as results.
record.test_reason: The study uses pretrained or self-trained SAEs as one component of its latent-knowledge elicitation pipeline (MechELK). It reports only elicitation accuracy, detection and false-positive rates for its method and baselines. SAE-Probe is a baseline, and the 'w/o SAE' result is an ablation of the authors' own pipeline. Neither measures whether features are spread across neurons, whether an SAE recovers the model's sparse features, or any superposition geometry. Superposition (Elhage et al. 2022) is only cited as motivation. This is T4: the finding is used as a tool, and only the method's own performance is reported.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that the Locate-Verify-Elicit pipeline (SAE features, activation patching, CKS causal verification, representation engineering) elicits latent knowledge better than baselines. They report 84.7% average elicitation accuracy (+6.2% over CCS), 78.3% identification where outputs are wrong or evasive, and false positives down 34% vs direct probing. They make no conclusion about superposition.
record.recipe_differences: MechELK uses SAE feature decomposition, activation patching, causal verification, and inference-time representation intervention for latent-knowledge elicitation; it does not reproduce the original toy-model setup or measure its superposition geometry.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that layer selection, CKS threshold, and intervention strength affect elicitation outcomes; these are pipeline sensitivities, not tests of superposition geometry.

fits_no_version.finding: Of the 8.6% of MechELK failures on TruthfulQA (Llama-3-8B), 31.1% are attributed to SAE reconstruction error: the SAE fails to reconstruct the relevant features, typically for rare or compositional facts. The attribution procedure is not described.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE dictionaries have coverage gaps for rare or compositional knowledge (a possible bearing on V5 completeness, but measured only as an unexplained failure-mode category of a downstream pipeline).

record.problems: The evidence is limited to selected LLMs and latent-knowledge benchmarks, so it does not establish general SAE feature recoverability. The paper reports SAE reconstruction error and knowledge fragmentation as failure modes. Standard deviations are reported for some results over 3 seeds, but not for the SAE-Probe values in Table 1.
record.rows_left_out: Other methods' aggregate elicitation metrics and the paraphrase-direction consistency scores were omitted because they evaluate the MechELK pipeline or recovered knowledge directions rather than SAE feature recovery as a representation claim.

untested.parts: No toy models, no feature-to-dimension capacity experiments, no sparsity transition or geometry.
No test of capacity competition as the cause of polysemanticity.
No test of alternative causes of polysemanticity.
No measurement of features spread across neurons, and no evaluation of SAE feature recovery (reconstruction, interpretability, sparsity) as a representation claim. SAE use is only instrumental.
No test of completeness, stability or canonicity of SAE features. Paraphrase consistency concerns the pipeline's knowledge directions, not dictionary units.
No comparison of 1-D vs multi-dimensional features.

record.verdict_notes: Internal inconsistencies worth flagging. Figure 4 legend gives means of 0.90/0.66/0.52, while the text and caption give 0.89/0.68/0.61. Table 5 reports Mistral-7B TruthfulQA and Quirky LM results and Llama-70B DAB results that are absent from Table 1. Figure 5 includes a 13B model not listed among the evaluated models. Section 4.4 says the layer distribution covers all TruthfulQA queries, but the figure shows TruthfulQA and DAB. The stated 34% FPR reduction does not match 28.4 to 12.7 (about 55%). The reader's V4 'supports' label is dropped because no row measures V4.

versions.untested_parts: No test of feature-over-capacity toy networks, overlap geometry, sparsity-dependent transitions, or regular geometry.
No test of polysemanticity as a consequence of capacity competition or of dedicated dimensions for important features.
No test of alternative causes of polysemanticity or whether polysemanticity is evidence for superposition.
Tests SAE-feature use for eliciting latent knowledge in selected LLMs and datasets; does not measure neuron-level feature spreading, general feature coverage, or superposition geometry.

Does not test whether SAE features are complete, canonical, or stable units of model representation. Its paraphrase consistency measure concerns recovered knowledge directions, not the SAE dictionary's units.
Uses feature directions but does not compare one-dimensional with multidimensional feature representations.

rows.note: Shows SAE-derived activations support latent-knowledge readout in this setting; it does not establish general feature coverage or superposition.
rows.check: Baseline method's task accuracy in a method comparison (Table 1). Elicitation accuracy of an SAE-feature probe does not measure feature recovery or distributed representation, so it cannot bear on V4. Subject is Llama-3-8B.

conditions.value: full MechELK versus w/o SAE (use raw activations)

rows.note: The authors report a 4.9% performance drop without SAE decomposition. This isolates a contribution to this pipeline, not a general claim about superposition.
rows.check: Ablation of the study's own pipeline: 82.3 full vs 77.4 without SAE. It shows SAE decomposition helps this method, not that the LLM contains recoverable sparse features. This is the study's own method compared with variants, so it should not be a claim row.

reader_labels.condition: SAE-Probe on the reported TruthfulQA, Quirky LM, and DAB model-dataset settings; TruthfulQA Llama-3-8B ablation
reader_labels.reason: SAE-derived features support latent-knowledge readout in the reported settings, and removing SAE decomposition reduces TruthfulQA accuracy (r1-r7).
